subject.title: feat(skills): add option to disable ~/.agents/skills scanning for Claude Code coexistence

question: Should OpenClaw add a public opt-out for `.agents/skills` discovery, and should that opt-out be source-id based or directory/path based?
rationale: The source-repro is clear, but the fix creates new `skills.load` config surface and changes behavior intentionally introduced for cross-agent skill discovery.

options.title: Add source-id opt-out
options.body: Introduce a documented default-on `skills.load` source-disable list for `agents-skills-personal` and `agents-skills-project`, then wire it through discovery, watchers, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Use existing allowlists only
options.body: Keep source discovery always-on and document `agents.defaults.skills` or per-agent `skills: []` as the supported way to avoid prompt exposure.

options.title: Defer to broader skill selection
options.body: Leave this open until maintainers design on-demand or intent-based skill selection that reduces large skill catalogs without another source toggle.

recommendation.title: Add source-id opt-out
recommendation.body: Introduce a documented default-on `skills.load` source-disable list for `agents-skills-personal` and `agents-skills-project`, then wire it through discovery, watchers, docs, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the affected `.agents/skills` discovery behavior and tests, making them the clearest history-linked reviewer for source semantics.
